bio.content: Olivia Isabel Rodrigo (born February 20, 2003) is an American singer-songwriter and actress. She began her acting career as a child, appearing in commercials and the direct-to-video film "An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success" (2015). She gained recognition for her roles as Paige Olvera in the Disney Channel series "Bizaardvark" (2016–2019) and Nini Salazar-Roberts in the Disney+ series "High School Musical: The Musical: The Series" (2019–2022). Rodrigo transitioned to music and signed with Geffen Records in 2020. Her debut studio album, "Sour" (2021), reached number one on the US Billboard 200 and several international charts. The album was preceded by the singles "Drivers License", "Deja Vu", and "Good 4 U", with "Drivers License" and "Good 4 U" reaching number one on the Billboard Hot 100. Her music career was documented in the Disney+ film "Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U" (2022). Her second studio album, "Guts" (2023), debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 and produced the single "Vampire", which also topped the Billboard Hot 100. Her third studio album, "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love" (2026), produced the number-one single "Drop Dead". Rodrigo became the first artist to have the lead single from each of her first three studio albums debut at number one on the Billboard Hot 100. Rodrigo's awards include three Grammy Awards, four MTV Video Music Awards, and seven Billboard Music Awards. She was named Time's Entertainer of the Year in 2021, Billboard's Woman of the Year in 2022, and ASCAP's Pop Music Songwriter of the Year in 2022 and 2024. Olivia Isabel Rodrigo was born on February 20, 2003, in Murrieta, California, to Jennifer Rodrigo, a school teacher, and Chris Rodrigo, a family therapist. She is an only child and grew up in Temecula, California. Rodrigo was born with partial hearing loss in her left ear. She is of Filipino American heritage through her father's family, whose ancestors emigrated from the Philippines. Her mother has German and Irish ancestry. Rodrigo grew up listening to alternative rock music from artists including No Doubt, Pearl Jam, the White Stripes, and Green Day. Rodrigo attended Lisa J. Mails Elementary School in Murrieta, where she participated in musical theatre activities. She began vocal lessons at age five, piano lessons at age nine, and later learned guitar. She became interested in songwriting after listening to country music by Taylor Swift. Her first screen appearance was in a 2010 Old Navy commercial. In 2015, Rodrigo made her acting debut as Grace Thomas in "An American Girl: Grace Stirs Up Success". In 2016, she moved to Los Angeles after being cast as Paige Olvera in "Bizaardvark", a role she played for three seasons. From 2019 to 2022, she starred as Nini Salazar-Roberts in "High School Musical: The Musical: The Series". She contributed songs to the series, including "All I Want", which was released in 2019. She left the series after its third season to focus on her music career. In 2020, Rodrigo signed with Geffen Records. Her debut single, "Drivers License", was released on January 8, 2021, and was co-written with producer Dan Nigro. The song became a worldwide commercial success, debuting at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and reaching the top position in several other countries. Her follow-up single, "Deja Vu", was released in April 2021 and reached the top ten of the Billboard Hot 100. "Good 4 U", released in May 2021, became her second number-one single. "Sour" was released on May 21, 2021. The album received positive reviews and topped the Billboard 200 for five weeks. In June 2021, Rodrigo released the concert film "Sour Prom" on YouTube. She was named Time's Entertainer of the Year in December 2021. "Sour" was among the best-selling albums of 2021 internationally, and "Drivers License" was among the year's most successful singles. Rodrigo supported "Sour" with the Sour Tour, which ran from April to July 2022 across North America and Europe. Her documentary film "Olivia Rodrigo: Driving Home 2 U" was released in March 2022. At the 64th Annual Grammy Awards, she won Best New Artist, Best Pop Vocal Album for "Sour", and Best Pop Solo Performance for "Drivers License". Rodrigo released her second studio album, "Guts", on September 8, 2023. She described the album as exploring themes of personal growth and self-discovery. The album's lead single, "Vampire", was released in June 2023 and became her third Billboard Hot 100 number-one single. The single "Bad Idea Right?" also reached the top ten in the United States and the United Kingdom. The song "Can't Catch Me Now", released for the film "The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" (2023), received the Hollywood Music in Media Award for Best Original Song in a Sci-Fi, Fantasy or Horror Film. To promote "Guts", Rodrigo embarked on the Guts World Tour from February 2024 to July 2025, with concerts in North America, Europe, Asia, and Oceania. A deluxe edition of the album, titled "Guts (Spilled)", was released in March 2024. In 2024, Rodrigo appeared with No Doubt at Coachella, performing the band's song "Bathwater". She later released the concert film "Olivia Rodrigo: Guts World Tour" on Netflix in October 2024. In 2025, Rodrigo performed at several music festivals, including Governors Ball, BST Hyde Park, Glastonbury Festival, and Lollapalooza Chicago. At Glastonbury, she performed with Robert Smith of the Cure, singing "Just Like Heaven" and "Friday I'm in Love". At Lollapalooza Chicago, she performed with Weezer, playing "Buddy Holly" and "Say It Ain't So". She also appeared in the documentary film "Lilith Fair: Building a Mystery – The Untold Story" (2025) and performed "We're Going to Be Friends" by the White Stripes with Feist at the White Stripes' Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony. Rodrigo announced her third studio album, "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love", in April 2026. Its lead single, "Drop Dead", was released later that month and debuted at number one on the Billboard Hot 100. The album was released on June 12, 2026, and debuted at number one on both the Billboard 200 and the UK Albums Chart. It became her third consecutive US number-one album. In 2026, Rodrigo performed "Drop Dead" live for the first time during a surprise appearance at Coachella. She announced the Unraveled Tour in support of "You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love", scheduled to run from September 2026 to May 2027. She also appeared as host and musical guest on "Saturday Night Live" in May 2026, performing "Drop Dead" and debuting the song "Begged". At Primavera Sound in June 2026, she performed the unreleased song "What's Wrong with Me" with Robert Smith. Later that month, she announced Daisy Chain Fields, an all-female music festival scheduled for August 2026 in Irvine, California, with proceeds benefiting charities supporting women and girls.
